portion_doctrine: Segment 11 is a transcript excerpt from Alex Hormozi on framework-building methodology and content strategy. The core insight: frameworks emerge from pattern-matching across repetitive work, not from first-principles thinking. Core method: (1) drink in tons of data from past work (e.g., 35 YouTube intros), (2) write down all variables/outcomes, (3) find the common denominator across all instances, (4) name it with mnemonic power (promise/path/plan, five horsemen retention). Controversy is reach-neutral beyond CTR; cancellation is a myth if you maintain audience access and keep producing. Agency-to-in-house transition: pay twice during overlap until in-house beats external; find agencies by talking to 10 and ranking by coherence, not bidding. Best agencies don't need to run ads (signal of demand proof). Content volume scales from committed-to-what-you-can baseline up, quality-first. Niche content drives product-market fit regardless of view count.
operating_rules: Framework extraction: (1) watch/analyze 20-35 instances of the task, (2) list all variables, (3) find commonalities across all instances, (4) distill to 3-5 core things that appear in ALL instances, (5) name with mnemonic/acronym
Agency to in-house: overlapping pay period is normal; tell agencies 'I will beat you' and replace when internal team outperforms external
Volume scales from baseline commitment; learn quality first before ramping volume
Niche content (low view count) drives product-market fit; not all reach matters
Cancellation is myth if you maintain platform access and keep producing; R Kelly canceled because he stopped content too
named_methods: Five Horsemen Retention (gym retention framework derived from 20-gym study)
Talk to 10 agencies, rank coherence, no bidding (discovery method)
numbers: 35 YouTube videos analyzed to extract intro patterns
20 gyms with sub-3% monthly churn interviewed for retention framework
20+ retention tactics per gym individually, but only 5 in common across all 20
3-5 core commonalities extracted from any dataset (rule of thumb)
specific_tactics: To find gym retention framework: filtered for gyms with <3% monthly churn x6-8 months, got 20 qualified gyms, interviewed all, found 5 retention tactics in common
To find creative directors: talk to 10, observe who has clarity, offer referrals to good ones (signal: best agencies have more work than they can handle)
skills: Naming frameworks with mnemonic power (branded methodology)
gates: Before scaling volume: quality proven at baseline commitment
Before declaring framework: verified commonalities across minimum N samples (not outliers, not isolated successes)
Before replacing external agency: internal team must beat external on measurable axis
contradictions: High-view content vs. niche-content product-market-fit: statement that 'niche content even if it doesn't get many views' drives customer acquisition seems to contradict earlier CTR/reach logic, but resolved by: CTR matters for feed algorithm; PMF customers come from niche positioning regardless of reach
weird_gold: Cancellation narrative is inverted: 'You can only be canceled if you stop making content.' Implies media permanence + continuous production is the ultimate defense (not audience size, not reputation management, not apology)
Best agencies signal via absence of advertising (more work than can handle). Flipped buyer-seller power dynamic: scarcity signals quality, not marketing spend
Framework naming trick: promise/path/plan share same letter (P), making it memorable. Mnemonic > clever = the actual design principle
